sources.entry: LoginLlama - Enhance Security with LoginLlama's Suspicious Login Detection #freemium

summary.name: LoginLlama
summary.one_liner: LoginLlama is a login risk-scoring API that rates each login from 0 to 10 for account takeover, credential stuffing, and bot traffic so an app can allow, step up to MFA, or block.
use_cases: Scoring each login before a session is issued
Flagging logins from Tor or VPN exit nodes
Detecting logins from new devices or locations
summary.what_it_does: LoginLlama is called after a successful password check, receiving the user, IP address, and user agent, and returns a 0-10 risk score along with codes explaining what triggered it. Signals mentioned include impossible travel, Tor and VPN exit nodes, new devices and browsers, new locations for a given user, and bots or headless browsers. The app decides what to do based on its own thresholds, such as requiring MFA or blocking when the score is above 5 in the sample code. The page states a response time under 500ms and says it fails open, so the login proceeds if the service errors or times out. SDKs are listed for Node.js/Next.js/Express, Python, and PHP/Laravel, and the page offers a prompt for coding agents to install and wire it up.
notable: Returns a 0-10 risk score plus the specific risk codes behind it
Fails open so real users are never locked out if the service is down
Single API call placed before the login is finalized, sub-500ms response per the page
caveats: Free tier covers 1,000 checks a month; higher volumes need paid Professional or Enterprise plans
Plan limits and prices beyond the free tier are not stated in the page text
Requires an API key and a signup account
